title: Understand Ratios
contentObjective: I can write and describe a ratio that compares two quantities.
languageObjective: I can explain a comparison using the words ratio, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and colon notation.

noticeAndWonder.context: The recipe shows the ingredients needed to make one batch of sparkling cranberry-apple fruit drink. How can you describe the relationship between the apple juice and the fruit drink? between the apple juice and sparkling water?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Middle School Fundraiser
revealWordProblem.text: Some sixth-grade students will make 50 bags of honey granola to sell at a fundraising event using the recipe shown. They will put 2 cups of granola in each bag and will sell each bag for $5. Choose one question to answer. Question 1: How many cups of rolled oats will the students need to buy? Question 2: One pound of almonds costs $9.99 and has 3 cups of almonds. How much will the students need to budget for almonds?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Question 1: The recipe makes 6 cups of granola using 4 cups of rolled oats, so rolled oats to total granola is a 4:6 ratio. The students need 50 bags × 2 cups = 100 cups of granola in all. Scaling the ratio: 100 ÷ 6 × 4 = 66 2/3 cups of rolled oats. They need to buy about 66 2/3 cups of rolled oats.

turnAndTalk.question: Chef Reyes's drink recipe uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water. How would you describe how these two ingredient amounts compare?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The recipe uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water.

stems.en: For every ___ cups of apple juice there are ___ cups of sparkling water.
stems.es: Por cada ___ tazas de jugo de manzana hay ___ tazas de agua con gas.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer names that apple juice and sparkling water are being compared and states the relationship as 3 to 2 (or 'for every 3 apple juice, 2 sparkling water'), not just that there is more apple juice.
turnAndTalk.extend: Would the ratio still describe the same recipe if you said it as sparkling water to apple juice instead of apple juice to sparkling water? Justify why the order changes the ratio but not the recipe.
extendStems: The order matters because ___, so apple juice to sparkling water (___) is different from sparkling water to apple juice (___).
Both describe the same recipe because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When you sorted the board statements, what made something a ratio instead of NOT a ratio (like '12 cookies on the tray')?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A ratio compares two quantities, but '12 cookies' is only one amount.

stems.en: This is a ratio because it compares ___ to ___.
stems.es: Esto es una razón porque compara ___ con ___.

stems.en: This is NOT a ratio because it only ___.
stems.es: Esto NO es una razón porque solo ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for the idea that a ratio must compare two quantities (using 'to', 'for every', 'out of', or a colon), while a single count or a description is not a comparison.
turnAndTalk.extend: Critique this claim: 'The oven is set to 350°F is a ratio because it has the word to in it.' Is the student right? Defend your answer.
extendStems: The student is wrong because the word 'to' alone does not ___; a ratio must ___.
350°F is just ___, not a comparison of ___ and ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The cafeteria wants 3 main dishes for every 2 side dishes. How is this the same kind of thinking as Chef Reyes's apple-juice-to-sparkling-water ratio?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Both use a ratio to keep two amounts in the same comparison.

stems.en: This is like our ratio work because ___ and ___ are compared.
stems.es: Esto es como nuestro trabajo con razones porque se comparan ___ y ___.

stems.en: The ratio of main dishes to side dishes is ___.
stems.es: La razón de platos principales a guarniciones es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer identifies the 3:2 part-to-part ratio and explains that the cafeteria keeps that comparison the same even when amounts grow, just like the recipe.
turnAndTalk.extend: If the cafeteria has 10 side dishes, generalize how you could figure out the main dishes — and explain why simply 'adding 1 more main than side' would NOT work.
extendStems: I can scale the ratio 3:2 by ___, so 10 sides means ___ mains.
Adding 1 each time does not work because a ratio must ___, not ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Understand Ratios, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A ratio compares two quantities, and the order you write them in matters.

stems.en: This is a ratio because it compares ___ to ___.
stems.es: Esto es una razón porque compara ___ con ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.1 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: Use a ratio to compare two quantities by division.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar una razón para comparar dos cantidades mediante la división.
vocabulary.visual: 3 red tiles to 5 blue tiles can be written 3:5 or 3/5.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of two quantities, like 3 to 5, is a ___.

examples.why: A single number does not compare two quantities.

vocabulary.definition: Looking at two or more amounts to see how they are related.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar dos o más cantidades para ver cómo se relacionan.
vocabulary.visual: 5 eggs vs. 3 eggs — which recipe uses more?
vocabulary.cloze: Showing how two amounts relate to each other is a ___.

examples.why: It looks at two amounts to see how they relate.
It states a single amount without relating it to anything.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing one part of a group to another part.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una parte de un grupo con otra parte.
vocabulary.visual: 3 cups flour : 2 cups sugar (ingredient to ingredient)
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares one part of a group to another part is a ___ ratio.

examples.why: It compares one part to another part.
That compares a part to the whole.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing one part to the whole group.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una parte con todo el grupo.
vocabulary.visual: 3 cups flour out of 5 cups total → 3:5
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares one part of a group to the total is a ___ ratio.

examples.why: It compares a part to the whole group.
That compares a part to another part.

vocabulary.definition: Writing a ratio with two dots between the numbers, like 3:2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Escribir una razón con dos puntos entre los números, como 3:2.
vocabulary.cloze: Writing a ratio with a colon, like 3:5, is using ___.

examples.why: It uses a colon between the two numbers being compared.
It uses words instead of a colon, so it is not colon notation.

launch.narrative: Welcome to Chef Academy! Head Chef Reyes is teaching new students how to read recipes like a pro. Her sparkling cranberry-apple fruit drink calls for 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water. Before the students can mix the drink, they need to understand how these ingredient amounts compare to each other.
noticePrompts: What two ingredients are being compared in the recipe?
How could you describe the relationship between apple juice and sparkling water?
Is the amount of apple juice more than, less than, or equal to the amount of sparkling water?
wonderPrompts: What if we compared the sparkling water to the apple juice instead — would the ratio change?
Could we compare one ingredient to the total amount of both?
launch.contextImage: A kitchen counter with measuring cups showing 3 cups of apple juice and 2 cups of sparkling water beside a recipe card

conceptIntro.heading: What is a ratio?
conceptIntro.intro: A ratio compares two amounts. It tells how much of one thing there is for another thing.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A ratio compares two quantities, and the order you write them in matters.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Chef Reyes uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water.
I am comparing two amounts: apple juice and sparkling water.
I write apple juice to sparkling water, in that order, as 3 to 2.
In colon notation I write it as 3:2.
So the ratio of apple juice to sparkling water is 3:2.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A bowl has 4 apples and 1 orange. What two amounts are we comparing?
We write apples to oranges in order: 4 to 1.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next you will sort the chef's statements into ratios and not-ratios.
Remember: a real ratio compares two amounts.

explore.instructions: Chef Reyes wrote several comparisons on the board. Sort them into two groups: statements that ARE ratios and statements that are NOT ratios.

items.text: 4 eggs for every 1 stick of butter
5 red apples out of 8 total apples
There are 12 cookies on the tray

discourse.prompt: What makes something a ratio? How did you decide which statements to sort into each group?
discourse.sentenceFrame: A ratio compares ___ to ___ using words like ___ or symbols like ___.

optional.stem: Prep Bowl A: Chef Reyes stirs 7 cups of flour with 4 cups of water to make dough. What is the part-to-part ratio of flour to water?
optional.explanation: Part-to-part compares the two ingredients in the order named. Flour to water = 7 to 4, written 7:4.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
11 is the total number of cups, not an ingredient. Part-to-part compares the two ingredients themselves.
optional.stemEs: Tazón de preparación A: el chef Reyes mezcla 7 tazas de harina con 4 tazas de agua para hacer masa. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a parte de harina a agua?
optional.explanationEs: Parte a parte compara los dos ingredientes en el orden en que se nombran. Harina a agua = 7 a 4, escrito 7:4.
hints: A ratio compares two amounts in the exact order the question names them.
Part-to-part compares one ingredient directly to the other ingredient, so there is no total to add here.
The question names flour first, so 7 goes in the first spot — now decide which amount belongs after the colon.
hintsEs: Una razón compara dos cantidades en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.
Parte a parte compara un ingrediente directamente con el otro, así que aquí no hay que sumar ningún total.
La pregunta nombra primero la harina, así que el 7 va en el primer lugar; ahora decide qué cantidad va después de los dos puntos.

optional.stem: A class has 5 chefs and 7 helpers (12 total). What is the part-to-whole ratio of chefs to the whole class?
optional.explanation: The whole class is 5 + 7 = 12 students. Part-to-whole compares one part to the total, so chefs to whole class is 5:12.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This is a correct part-to-whole ratio, but for the helpers. Check which group the question asks you to compare to the whole class.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
optional.stemEs: Una clase tiene 5 chefs y 7 ayudantes (12 en total). ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de chefs a la clase completa?
optional.explanationEs: La clase completa son 5 + 7 = 12 estudiantes. Parte a todo compara una parte con el total, así que chefs a la clase completa es 5:12.
hints: A part-to-whole ratio compares one group to the total group, not to the other part.
Find the whole first by adding the two groups together.
The whole class is 5 + 7 = 12 students. Now decide which number the question names first and put it in front of the colon.
hintsEs: Una razón parte a todo compara un grupo con el grupo total, no con la otra parte.
Primero halla el total sumando los dos grupos.
La clase completa son 5 + 7 = 12 estudiantes. Ahora decide qué número nombra primero la pregunta y colócalo antes de los dos puntos.

optional.stem: “For every” language: Chef Reyes says, “My glaze uses 9 spoons of honey for every 4 spoons of lemon.” Written in colon notation, the ratio of honey to lemon is:
optional.explanation: “For every 9 honey to 4 lemon” is a part-to-part comparison. In colon notation, honey to lemon is 9:4.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
13 is the total number of spoons, so this compares the whole mixture to the lemon. “For every” language compares the two ingredients themselves.
optional.stemEs: Lenguaje de «por cada»: el chef Reyes dice: «Mi glaseado usa 9 cucharadas de miel por cada 4 cucharadas de limón». En notación con dos puntos, la razón de miel a limón es:
optional.explanationEs: «Por cada 9 de miel a 4 de limón» es una comparación parte a parte. En notación con dos puntos, miel a limón es 9:4.
hints: “For every” is ratio language — it compares one amount directly to another amount.
Colon notation writes the quantity named first, then a colon, then the quantity named second.
The sentence names honey first with 9 spoons, so 9 goes before the colon — now decide which number belongs after it.
hintsEs: «Por cada» es lenguaje de razón: compara una cantidad directamente con otra cantidad.
La notación con dos puntos escribe primero la cantidad que se nombra primero, luego los dos puntos y después la segunda cantidad.
La oración nombra primero la miel con 9 cucharadas, así que el 9 va antes de los dos puntos; ahora decide qué número va después.

optional.instructions: Sort each kitchen comparison: is it a PART-TO-PART ratio (one part to another part) or a PART-TO-WHOLE ratio (one part to the total)?

items.text: 6 cups of broth to 5 cups of noodles
6 spicy dishes out of 11 total dishes
8 forks to 3 spoons on the prep table
3 burnt cookies out of 12 total cookies
4 vegetarian plates out of 10 total plates

optional.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
optional.explanation: The phrase 'out of ... total' marks a part-to-whole ratio: 6 spicy dishes out of 11, 3 burnt cookies out of 12, and 4 vegetarian plates out of 10 each compare one piece to the entire group. The other three cards compare one piece to another piece — broth to noodles, forks to spoons, savory bites to sweet bites — so they are part-to-part.
optional.explanationEs: La frase 'out of ... total' marca una razón parte a todo: 6 platillos picantes de 11, 3 galletas quemadas de 12 y 4 platos vegetarianos de 10 comparan una porción con el grupo completo. Las otras tres tarjetas comparan una porción con otra porción (caldo con fideos, tenedores con cucharas, bocados salados con bocados dulces), así que son parte a parte.
optional.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada comparación de la cocina: ¿es una razón PARTE A PARTE (una parte con otra parte) o PARTE A TODO (una parte con el total)?

optional.label: Plating Match: Match each kitchen context to the ratio that describes it in colon form.

pairs.term: 5 plain rolls out of 9 total rolls
2 grilled skewers out of 7 total skewers

optional.explanation: Each match keeps the numbers in the order the words name them, written with a colon: 4 lemons for every 3 limes is 4:3, 5 plain rolls out of 9 total rolls is 5:9, 8 clean pans to 1 dirty pan is 8:1, and 2 grilled skewers out of 7 total skewers is 2:7. Two of these compare a part to the whole, but colon form is written exactly the same way.
optional.explanationEs: Cada emparejamiento mantiene los números en el orden en que los nombran las palabras, escritos con dos puntos: 4 limones por cada 3 limas es 4:3, 5 panecillos simples de 9 panecillos en total es 5:9, 8 sartenes limpias a 1 sartén sucia es 8:1, y 2 brochetas asadas de 7 brochetas en total es 2:7. Dos de estas comparan una parte con el todo, pero la forma con dos puntos se escribe exactamente igual.
optional.labelEs: Emplatado: Une cada contexto de la cocina con la razón que lo describe en forma de dos puntos.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Chef Mateo's Pizza Topping Ratio

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A pizza has 6 olives, 2 peppers, and 4 tomato slices. Write the part-to-whole ratio of peppers to the total toppings.

workedExample.label: Write the ratio
workedExample.work: Chef Mateo writes peppers to total as 2:6.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The ratio of peppers to total toppings is 2:6.

optional.correctWork: Part-to-whole compares the part to the WHOLE (12), not to one other part. The peppers are 2 and the whole is 12, so the correct ratio is 2:12.
hints: Look at Step 3. A part-to-whole ratio should use the total from Step 2.
Chef Mateo used 6 (just the olives) instead of the whole. The whole is 12, so peppers to total is 2:12.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: la razón de ingredientes de la pizza del chef Mateo
optional.explanation: Chef Mateo counted the whole correctly: 6 + 2 + 4 = 12 toppings. The error is in the ratio — he compared the 2 peppers to the 6 olives instead of to the whole pizza. A part-to-whole ratio uses the total, so peppers to total toppings is 2:12.
optional.explanationEs: El chef Mateo contó bien el total: 6 + 2 + 4 = 12 ingredientes. El error está en la razón: comparó los 2 pimientos con las 6 aceitunas en vez de compararlos con la pizza completa. Una razón parte a todo usa el total, así que pimientos a ingredientes totales es 2:12.

approaching.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
approaching.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
5 is the total number of cups, not the amount of cream. This compares the whole recipe to one part instead of milk to cream.
hints: Re-read the question: it asks for milk to cream, in that exact order.
In a ratio, the amount named first goes first. Find the milk amount and the cream amount before you write anything.
Underline the two amounts: milk = 4 cups, cream = 1 cup. Write them in the same order the question names them.
approaching.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de leche y 1 taza de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de leche a crema?
approaching.explanationEs: Una razón compara cantidades en el orden que se indica. Leche a crema = 4 a 1, o 4:1.

approaching.stem: Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
approaching.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This compares bananas to strawberries, which is part-to-part. A part-to-whole ratio needs the total number of pieces of fruit as the second number.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: Notice the word 'total' — this is a part-to-WHOLE ratio, not banana-to-strawberry.
First find the total fruit by adding strawberries and bananas. Then compare bananas to that total.
Add 6 + 2 to get the total fruit. Then write the bananas' number first, followed by that total.
approaching.stemEs: El chef Reyes usa 6 fresas y 2 plátanos en un batido. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de plátanos a fruta total?
approaching.explanationEs: Fruta total = 6 + 2 = 8. La razón parte a todo de plátanos a fruta total es 2:8.

approaching.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls. What is the part-to-part ratio of boys to girls?
approaching.explanation: Boys = 30 − 18 = 12. Part-to-part ratio of boys to girls = 12:18. (Order matters!)
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
You found the number of boys correctly, but 30 is the whole class. That makes this part-to-whole, and the question asks boys compared to girls.
hints: The problem tells you girls (18) and the whole class (30) — but it asks about BOYS to girls.
Find the number of boys first by subtracting the girls from the class total. Then write boys first, girls second.
Subtract 30 − 18 to find the boys. Put that number first in the ratio, then 18 for the girls.
approaching.stemEs: En una clase de 30 estudiantes, 18 son niñas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a parte de niños a niñas?
approaching.explanationEs: Niños = 30 − 18 = 12. La razón parte a parte de niños a niñas = 12:18. (¡El orden importa!)

approaching.stem: A pet store has 5 dogs and 9 cats. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
approaching.explanation: The ratio of dogs to cats compares dogs first, then cats: 5 to 9, or 5:9.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
14 is the total number of pets, and here it is written first. Check both the order of the words and whether the question asks about a total at all.
hints: Re-read: the question asks for dogs to cats, in that order.
A ratio only uses the two amounts being compared — don't add them together. Match the order to the words.
Dogs are named first, so their count (5) starts the ratio. Then write the cats' count after the colon.
approaching.stemEs: Una tienda de mascotas tiene 5 perros y 9 gatos. ¿Cuál es la razón de perros a gatos?
approaching.explanationEs: La razón de perros a gatos compara primero los perros y después los gatos: 5 a 9, o 5:9.

approaching.instructions: Sort each statement: does it describe a ratio or NOT describe a ratio?

items.text: There are 15 chairs in the room

approaching.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: A ratio must COMPARE two amounts. Ask each card: does it mention two quantities, or just one?
Look for compare words like 'for every' or 'to.' A single count ('15 chairs') or an opinion ('delicious') compares nothing.
Test the first card: does '7 pencils for every 3 erasers' name TWO amounts being compared? That answer tells you its pile.
approaching.explanation: A ratio compares two quantities, so '7 pencils for every 3 erasers' and '10 red beads to 4 blue beads' are ratios — each names two amounts, joined by the words 'for every' and 'to'. 'There are 15 chairs in the room' reports a single count with nothing to compare it to, and 'The pizza was delicious' is an opinion with no quantities at all.
approaching.explanationEs: Una razón compara dos cantidades, así que '7 pencils for every 3 erasers' y '10 red beads to 4 blue beads' sí son razones: cada una nombra dos cantidades, unidas por las palabras 'for every' y 'to'. 'There are 15 chairs in the room' informa una sola cantidad y no la compara con nada, y 'The pizza was delicious' es una opinión sin ninguna cantidad.
approaching.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada afirmación: ¿describe una razón o NO describe una razón?

approaching.title: Spot the Mistake — Order of a Ratio

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A salad bar has 5 bowls of soup and 8 sandwiches. Write the ratio of soup to sandwiches.

workedExample.label: Write the ratio
workedExample.work: A student writes the ratio of soup to sandwiches as 8:5.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The ratio of soup to sandwiches is 8:5.

approaching.correctWork: The order matters. The problem asks for soup to sandwiches, so soup (5) must come first: the correct ratio is 5:8, not 8:5.
hints: Look at Step 3. Which amount should be written first — soup or sandwiches?
Soup is named first, so the ratio is 5:8. The student reversed the order.
approaching.titleEs: Detecta el error: el orden de una razón
approaching.explanation: The amounts are identified correctly — soup is 5 and sandwiches is 8 — but the ratio is written backwards. A ratio lists the quantities in the order the words name them, and the question asks for soup to sandwiches, so soup comes first: 5:8. Writing 8:5 describes sandwiches to soup instead.
approaching.explanationEs: Las cantidades están bien identificadas (la sopa es 5 y los sándwiches son 8), pero la razón está escrita al revés. Una razón coloca las cantidades en el orden en que las nombran las palabras, y la pregunta pide sopa a sándwiches, así que la sopa va primero: 5:8. Escribir 8:5 describe sándwiches a sopa, que es otra cosa.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each statement — is it a part-to-part ratio or a part-to-whole ratio?

items.text: 3 boys to 5 girls in cooking class
4 vegetarian dishes out of 10 total dishes
3 sweet items out of 10 total items

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: Look for the words 'out of' or 'total' — those signal a comparison to the WHOLE group.
Ask each card: are BOTH numbers pieces of the group (part-to-part), or is the second number the whole group (part-to-whole)?
Try '3 boys to 5 girls': boys and girls are each just one part of the class — no total is named. Which pile does that point to?
onLevel.explanation: A part-to-part ratio compares one piece of a group to another piece: 3 boys to 5 girls, 2 cups sugar to 3 cups flour, and 7 savory items to 3 sweet items. A part-to-whole ratio compares one piece to the entire group, and the phrase 'out of ... total' gives it away: 5 girls out of 8 students, 4 vegetarian dishes out of 10, and 3 sweet items out of 10.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una razón parte a parte compara una porción del grupo con otra porción: 3 niños a 5 niñas, 2 tazas de azúcar a 3 tazas de harina, y 7 platillos salados a 3 dulces. Una razón parte a todo compara una porción con el grupo completo, y la frase 'out of ... total' lo delata: 5 niñas de 8 estudiantes, 4 platillos vegetarianos de 10 y 3 postres de 10.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada afirmación: ¿es una razón parte a parte o una razón parte a todo?

onLevel.stem: A fruit salad has 5 pieces of melon, 3 pieces of pineapple, and 2 grapes. What is the ratio of pineapple to melon?
onLevel.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
Think about which quantities should be in this ratio and their order.
You started with the pineapple, which fits the order — but 2 is the number of grapes. Re-read which two amounts the question compares.
hints: Three fruits are listed, but the question only compares pineapple and melon — the grapes are extra info.
Pick out just the two amounts you need, then write them in the order the question names: pineapple first.
Circle the pineapple count (3) and the melon count (5). Write them in the order 'pineapple to melon.'
onLevel.stemEs: Una ensalada de frutas tiene 5 trozos de melón, 3 trozos de piña y 2 uvas. ¿Cuál es la razón de piña a melón?
onLevel.explanationEs: La razón de piña a melón compara la piña (3) con el melón (5), así que la razón es 3:5.

onLevel.instructions: Complete the table by writing each ratio in all three forms.
hints: Look at the finished row: '4 cats to 7 dogs' becomes 4 to 7, then 4:7, then 4/7 — same numbers, three costumes.
Keep the numbers and their order the same in every column; only the symbols change (the word 'to', a colon, a fraction bar).
Start with row 2: which number comes first, the 9 red or the 15 total? Keep that order and just change the symbol in each column.
onLevel.explanation: The same ratio can wear three costumes without changing value: word form uses 'to', colon form uses a colon, and fraction form uses a fraction bar. The numbers and their order stay identical across the row, so '9 red out of 15 total' becomes 9 to 15, 9:15, and 9/15, and '5 wins to 3 losses' becomes 5 to 3, 5:3, and 5/3.
onLevel.explanationEs: La misma razón puede vestirse de tres formas sin cambiar de valor: en palabras se usa 'to', en la forma de dos puntos se usan los dos puntos, y en la forma de fracción se usa la barra de fracción. Los números y su orden se mantienen iguales en toda la fila, así que '9 red out of 15 total' se escribe 9 to 15, 9:15 y 9/15, y '5 wins to 3 losses' se escribe 5 to 3, 5:3 y 5/3.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Completa la tabla escribiendo cada razón en las tres formas.

onLevel.stem: A parking lot has 10 cars and 6 trucks. What is the part-to-whole ratio of trucks to total vehicles?
onLevel.explanation: Total vehicles = 10 + 6 = 16. The ratio of trucks to total is 6:16.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This compares trucks to cars, which is a part-to-part ratio. For part-to-whole you need 10 + 6 as the second number.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: The word 'total' means this is part-to-whole — compare trucks to ALL vehicles, not to cars.
First find the total number of vehicles by adding cars and trucks. The trucks' number goes first.
Add 10 + 6 to find the total vehicles. Then write 6 (the trucks) first and that total second.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estacionamiento tiene 10 autos y 6 camionetas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de camionetas al total de vehículos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Total de vehículos = 10 + 6 = 16. La razón de camionetas al total es 6:16.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake — Part-to-Whole Ratio

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A class has 9 boys and 6 girls. Write the part-to-whole ratio of girls to the whole class.

workedExample.label: Write the ratio
workedExample.work: A student writes girls to the whole class as 6:9.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The part-to-whole ratio of girls to the whole class is 6:9.

onLevel.correctWork: Part-to-whole compares the part to the WHOLE (15), not to the other part. There are 6 girls and 15 students total, so the correct ratio is 6:15.
hints: Look at Step 3. A part-to-whole ratio should use the total from Step 2.
The student used 9 (just the boys) instead of the whole. The whole is 15, so girls to the whole class is 6:15.
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error: razón parte a todo
onLevel.explanation: The whole is counted correctly: 9 + 6 = 15 students. The mistake is in the ratio itself — it compares the 6 girls to the 9 boys instead of to the whole class. A part-to-whole ratio has to use the total, so girls to the whole class is 6:15.
onLevel.explanationEs: El total está bien contado: 9 + 6 = 15 estudiantes. El error está en la razón misma: compara las 6 niñas con los 9 niños en vez de compararlas con toda la clase. Una razón parte a todo tiene que usar el total, así que niñas a toda la clase es 6:15.

extending.title: Find Aliya's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A trail mix has 6 almonds, 4 raisins, and 2 cashews. Write the ratio of raisins to total pieces.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The ratio of raisins to total is 4:8.

extending.correctWork: The total is 12, not 8. The correct ratio is 4:12.
hints: Look at Step 3. Does 8 match the total Aliya found in Step 2?
The total is 12 pieces, so the part-to-whole ratio should use 12, not 8.
extending.explanation: Aliya counted the total correctly: 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 pieces. But the ratio she wrote uses 8, which is not the total — it is only the almonds and raisins together. Comparing the 4 raisins to the whole 12 pieces gives 4:12.
extending.explanationEs: Aliya contó bien el total: 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 piezas. Pero la razón que escribió usa 8, que no es el total: son solo las almendras y las pasas juntas. Comparar las 4 pasas con las 12 piezas completas da 4:12.

extending.stem: A bag of marbles has 8 red, 6 blue, and 4 green marbles. Write three different ratios using these quantities: one part-to-part ratio, one part-to-whole ratio, and explain the difference.
extending.sampleAnswer: Part-to-part: red to blue = 8:6. Part-to-whole: green to total = 4:18. The difference is that part-to-part compares two individual groups, while part-to-whole compares one group to the entire collection (8 + 6 + 4 = 18).
extending.hint: Remember to explain which type each ratio is.
hints: You need THREE things: a part-to-part ratio, a part-to-whole ratio, and an explanation of how they differ.
Part-to-part compares two colors. Part-to-whole compares one color to ALL marbles — so you'll need the total first.
Start by finding the whole: add 8 + 6 + 4. Then pick any two colors for your part-to-part ratio, like red to blue.
extending.stemEs: Una bolsa de canicas tiene 8 canicas rojas, 6 azules y 4 verdes. Escribe tres razones distintas usando estas cantidades: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo, y explica la diferencia.
extending.explanation: A part-to-part ratio compares two groups to each other, such as red to blue, 8:6. A part-to-whole ratio compares one group to the total of 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 marbles, such as green to all marbles, 4:18. The difference is what the second number stands for: another part, or the entire set.
extending.explanationEs: Una razón parte a parte compara dos grupos entre sí, por ejemplo rojas a azules, 8:6. Una razón parte a todo compara un grupo con el total de 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 canicas, por ejemplo verdes a todas las canicas, 4:18. La diferencia está en lo que representa el segundo número: otra parte o el conjunto completo.

extending.instructions: A classroom has 12 boys and 8 girls. Sort each ratio statement as either CORRECT or INCORRECT.
extending.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: First figure out the class total from 12 boys and 8 girls — some cards secretly use it.
For each card, check two things: are the numbers right, AND does the order match the words (boys first if it says 'boys to')?
Test 'Boys to girls = 12:8': boys are 12, girls are 8, and boys are named first. Does the card's ratio match that order?
extending.explanation: With 12 boys and 8 girls, the class total is 20. 'Boys to girls = 12:8' is correct because boys are named first and there are 12 of them, and 'Girls to total = 8:20' correctly compares a part to the whole. 'Boys to total = 12:8' uses the girls instead of the 20-student total, and 'Girls to boys = 12:8' has the numbers reversed — it should be 8:12.
extending.explanationEs: Con 12 niños y 8 niñas, el total de la clase es 20. 'Boys to girls = 12:8' es correcta porque los niños se nombran primero y son 12, y 'Girls to total = 8:20' compara bien una parte con el todo. 'Boys to total = 12:8' usa a las niñas en vez del total de 20 estudiantes, y 'Girls to boys = 12:8' tiene los números invertidos: debería ser 8:12.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Understand Ratios is writing the ratio in the wrong order: when asked for the ratio of apple juice to sparkling water in a recipe that uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water, some students write 2:3 (sparkling water to apple juice) because they list the ingredients in whatever order comes to mind rather than the order the question asks for. The two ratios describe different drinks — 3:2 means 3 cups of juice for every 2 cups of water, while 2:3 would mean only 2 cups of juice for every 3 cups of water. Always match the order of your ratio to the order named in the question: "apple juice to sparkling water" means the apple juice number comes first, giving 3:2.

exitTicket.stem: A bag of trail mix contains 8 peanuts and 5 raisins. What is the ratio of raisins to total pieces?
exitTicket.explanation: Total pieces = 8 + 5 = 13. The ratio of raisins to total is 5:13.
choiceFeedback: That's peanuts to raisins — the question asks raisins to TOTAL.
That compares raisins to peanuts, not raisins to the whole bag.
You reversed it — put raisins first, then the total.
hints: Careful — this asks for raisins compared to ALL the pieces in the bag, not to the peanuts.
Find the total first by adding peanuts and raisins, then write the raisins' number before the total.
Add 8 + 5 to get the total pieces. Start the ratio with 5 (the raisins), then put that total after the colon.

questions.stem: Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
questions.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.

questions.stem: A pet store has 5 dogs and 9 cats. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
questions.explanation: The ratio of dogs to cats compares dogs first, then cats: 5 to 9, or 5:9.

questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls. What is the part-to-part ratio of boys to girls?
questions.explanation: Boys = 30 − 18 = 12. Part-to-part ratio of boys to girls = 12:18. (Order matters!)

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
questions.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
